assumptions: p is prime. At length n the abelian presentation has p*x_i=e_i*x_(i+1), e_i in {0,1}, for i<n-1, and p*x_(n-1)=0.
Transition maps discard the last digit; filtration is by vanishing initial digits, not necessarily p-adic powers.
The infinite model uses a single fixed edge sequence and its compatible truncations.
All-degree and infinite-limit arguments remain ordinary unverified proof obligations; finite results do not prove them.
No identification with TC, Tate, a motivic filtration or a cyclotomic Frobenius is asserted.
target: Determine how nearest-neighbour additive extension data changes the exponent despite identical associated graded, and whether bounded graded exponent plus complete separated filtration forces rational vanishing.
